prompt: A 28-year-old woman from rural Ghana presents with high fever, chills, headache, and sweating after several days of mosquito exposure near stagnant water. She looks pale and slightly jaundiced. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 19-year-old man from Manila develops high fever, severe headache behind the eyes, joint pain, nausea, and a maculopapular rash on day 3. He reports multiple mosquito bites last week. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 34-year-old woman from rural India presents with a 6-day history of high fever, abdominal pain, headache, and alternating constipation and diarrhea. She has a faint rash on her trunk. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 7-year-old boy living in a refugee camp in Bangladesh suddenly develops profuse watery diarrhea that looks like rice water, vomiting, and signs of dehydration after flooding in the area. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 42-year-old rice farmer in the Philippines reports fever, chills, muscle pain, headache, and yellowing of the eyes. He frequently works barefoot in flooded fields. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 29-year-old woman from Hanoi has a persistent productive cough for over three weeks, fever, night sweats, and mild weight loss. She reports a household contact with similar symptoms. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A 36-year-old HIV-positive man in Rwanda presents with fever, headache, confusion, and neck stiffness that developed over a few days. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old woman from rural Brazil presents with intermittent fever, fatigue, and an enlarged spleen. She has been working outdoors and frequently bitten by sandflies. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 30-year-old man from rural Morocco presents with a painless ulcer on his forearm that slowly enlarged over several weeks. He often works outdoors where sandflies are common. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old man from rural Mexico has fever, right upper abdominal pain, and weight loss two months after an episode of bloody diarrhea. Examination shows tender hepatomegaly. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old woman working on a tea plantation in Northeast Thailand presents with fever, severe headache, body aches, and a dark scab (eschar) on her leg surrounded by a rash. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old man who lives in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia attends your clinic complaining of a progressive skin eruption of the body and limbs for 1 year. The rash is not itchy or painful.  He has had no previous skin problems and no contact with a similarly affected person. His appearance gradually changed over 12 months. There is a papular and nodular eruption on the extensor aspects of the forearms, arms, thighs and trunk. Furthermore, there is a diffuse infiltration of the skin of the face and nodules on the pinnae, with madarosis (loss of eyebrows and eyelashes). There is no loss of sensation within the skin lesions and no sensory or motor loss in the hands or feet. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 34-year-old man from a high HIV-prevalence area in sub-Saharan Africa presents with a history of recurrent pneumonia. His chest X-ray reveals hilar lymphadenopathy, pleural effusions, and middle/lower lung infiltrates with minimal cavitation. A bronchoscopy confirms the presence of ulcerative mucosa and endobronchial polyps.

A young man in Central Africa, recently diagnosed with AIDS, presents with progressive violaceous skin nodules and hemoptysis (coughing up blood). A chest radiograph shows diffuse interstitial nodulation and hilar adenopathy. Bronchoscopy reveals characteristic pinkish, red, flat lesions on the bronchial walls that bleed easily.

A 50-year-old asymptomatic farmer from a Mediterranean country, who works closely with sheep and domesticated dogs, undergoes a routine chest X-ray. The image reveals a large, well-defined, homogenous nodule in the right lung lobe. A CT scan confirms it is a fluid-filled cyst. Calcification is notably absent, which is typical for pulmonary cysts.

A 38-year-old man from an endemic area in Asia presents with a chronic cough and dyspnea. He reports coughing up a "rusty, or chocolate-colored sputum." His dietary history includes eating raw freshwater crabs. A chest X-ray reveals multiple, patchy, ill-defined shadows and small cystic areas described as "bubbles." A sputum analysis confirms the diagnosis by identifying characteristic eggs.

A 55-year-old man, who served in the military in Vietnam 30 years ago, is now receiving immunosuppressive therapy for an unrelated condition. He presents with a long history of cough, low-grade fever, weight loss, and hemoptysis. His chest X-ray closely resembles pulmonary tuberculosis, showing an upper lobe infiltrate that shows cavitation. The diagnosis is confirmed by isolating B. pseudomallei from his sputum.

A 50-year-old slaughterhouse worker from the Mediterranean region presents to the clinic. He complains of fever, chills, aches and pains, and weakness, along with a mild cough. His chest radiograph is normal, though in rare cases, findings can include miliary infiltration or pleural effusion. Diagnosis is based on his occupational history, clinical features, and positive serological tests.

A 24-year-old man presents with an acute febrile illness after a kayaking trip in a tropical region, where he was exposed to contaminated water after a heavy rainstorm. He presents with fever, myalgias, and conjunctival suffusion. His condition is severe, presenting with high fever, intense jaundice, and bleeding, progressing to massive hemoptysis and respiratory failure.

A 33-year-old woman presents with a "flu-like illness" after exploring a cave known to house bats in the Midwestern United States. She reports an abrupt onset of fever, chills, substernal chest discomfort, a harsh, nonproductive cough, and headache. Radiography shows a single area of pneumonitis with enlarged ipsilateral hilar and mediastinal lymph nodes. Serologic tests (complement fixation) are positive.

A 28-year-old healthcare worker presents with sudden onset of high fever, severe headache, myalgia, and profound weakness after returning from an aid mission in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Over the next few days, she develops vomiting, diarrhea, conjunctival injection, and diffuse bleeding from venipuncture sites. Laboratory findings reveal thrombocytopenia and elevated liver enzymes. RT-PCR testing confirms infection with a filovirus.
A 12 year old girl with fever, reduced appetite, and pus-like oozing from her ear.
